question.prompt:
Given the four equations:

\[ \begin{aligned} (1)\quad&3y-2x=12,\\ (2)\quad&-2x-3y=10,\\ (3)\quad&3y+2x=12,\\ (4)\quad&2y+3x=10. \end{aligned} \]

The pair representing perpendicular lines is:

solutions.explanation:
Writing each equation with \(y\) alone reveals its slope. All four coefficients of \(y\) are nonzero, so every line has a finite slope:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(1)\quad y&=\frac23x+4,\\
(2)\quad y&=-\frac23x-\frac{10}{3},\\
(3)\quad y&=-\frac23x+4,\\
(4)\quad y&=-\frac32x+5.
\end{aligned}
\]
Two lines with finite slopes are perpendicular exactly when the product of their slopes is \(-1\). For equations (1) and (4),
\[
 \frac23\left(-\frac32\right)=-1.
\]
The remaining slope, \(-\frac23\), would require a perpendicular slope of \(\frac32\), which does not occur. Thus the perpendicular pair is (1) and (4), choice A.
solutions.title: Compare the slopes
